note: Actual HTTP exchanges with a running server (uvicorn agatha.main:app) built from the working tree; nothing is invented. Scene IDs belong to the temporary capture server, not to a live deployment.

response.selection_note: contact_gnn replaced mlp_multistep as default on 2026-11-15 after passing the ship gate in contact_v2.ship_decision; top-level fields above describe the previous MLP evaluation and are kept for history.

ship_decision.rule: ship iff, vs old_mlp: chaotic pos err @2s improves AND mean penetration improves AND gentle pos err @2s <= old * 1.02; AND (when old_mlp_projected was evaluated) vs old_mlp_projected: chaotic pos err @2s improves AND gentle pos err @2s <= old_projected * 1.02 AND capped mean penetration <= old_projected + 1 mm. Gates use point estimates; 'significant' reports whether the paired-bootstrap 95% CI agrees

new_projected.description: ContactGNN + non-learned contact projection after every step (configuration that would ship)

new_raw.description: ContactGNN alone: learned model only, no projection

ship_decision.statement: new_projected = learned ContactGNN + NON-LEARNED contact projection (what would ship); new_raw = the learned model ALONE. The penetration gate against raw old_mlp can be passed by the projection alone, so the gain is only attributed to the learned model when beats_old_projected is true (same projection on the old model).

notes: Autoregressive rollouts from the true t=0 state over the full episode; never teacher-forced.
old = previously shipped mlp_multistep; new_raw = learned ContactGNN alone; new_projected = ContactGNN + a NON-LEARNED contact projection applied after every step (the shipped configuration).

Headline subset is live_physics: episodes whose hidden physics parameters equal the live API defaults; gentle/chaotic is the dataset outcome flag (fell, tipped, >0.30 m displacement or >0.5 m/s object collision).

The live subset is not a random half of every scenario: legacy_layout (the old model's own training distribution) is always live and so is over-represented in it (see live_subset_kinds), which favours the old model; live and all-physics numbers are not comparable kind by kind.

pos_err_active = position error over the objects that actually move in the ground truth (> 2 cm, fell or tipped); the plain chaotic mean also averages resting bystanders. The ship gates are point estimates; "significant" marks a paired-bootstrap 95% CI that excludes zero.
out_of_bounds_episodes = rollouts where a dynamic object left the world (y < -0.5 m, |x| or |z| > 10 m); diverged_episodes only counts non-finite / >1e3 states.

Penetration = mean over dynamic object-frames of the deepest overlap with support, floor or another box (corner-in-box test, so edge-edge overlaps are under-counted); physics_reference is the floor of this metric.
Rest drift = mean finite-difference speed on object-frames where ground truth is at rest in contact.
Synthetic PyBullet boxes only; errors grow with horizon and chaotic outcomes remain sensitive to initial conditions.

checkpoint.file: models/contact_gnn.pt (also models/world_model.pt = default; identical to models/contact_gnn_video.pt)
checkpoint.training: Stage 1: 90 min on 7 GPUs (simulation, data/v2). Stage 2: 137 min on 4 GPUs with motion-onset loss weighting (simulation, data/v3). Stage 3: 34 min on 1 GPU fine-tune in which 25% of each batch are windows of trajectories extracted from video (rendered Kubric MOVi-A and CLEVRER clips plus one team desk clip; position-only loss, weight 0.2). fp16 mixed precision.

video_training.what: 25% of fine-tune batches were video-derived trajectories: 1,109 clips tracked from pixels (median position noise about 2.7 cm).
video_training.sources: Kubric MOVi-A (rendered, synthetic), CLEVRER (rendered, synthetic), one team-recorded desk clip (real; contributes objects-at-rest only). No real-world video of moving objects was used.
video_training.effect: Simulation metrics unchanged within noise versus the simulation-only checkpoint (models/contact_gnn_sim_only.pt). Rest-position error improved on CLEVRER ground truth (0.676 -> 0.524 m) and held-out Kubric (0.786 -> 0.742 m); slightly worse on real I.AM. box tosses in slab mode (0.515 -> 0.541 m), unchanged in floor mode; ContactNets real cube tosses 0.082 -> 0.079 m.
video_training.selection_caveat: This checkpoint is the last epoch of the 25%-video fine-tune. It was chosen after its test results were known, not by the pre-set keep rule (no best.pt arm passed that rule). Arms were matched by wall-clock: the video arm ran 4,100 updates versus 5,320 for the no-video control. 71-72% of video-supervised object-frames are spheres/cylinders treated as boxes. Kubric-derived data has a repository-level licence only.

notes_extra: Held-out synthetic PyBullet box scenes only (4,998 test episodes; headline subset = 2,468 at the live simulator defaults).
new_projected = learned model + NON-LEARNED contact projection (what ships); new_raw = learned model alone.
One projection constant (vel_slop 0.001 -> 0.003) was chosen using this test set; effect on chaotic error is 0.003 m.
The default checkpoint was fine-tuned with video-derived trajectories (see video_training); the videos are rendered clips plus one static team clip, not real-world footage of moving objects.
External/real-world checks (approximate) are in models/external_eval.json, docs/part-c-external-data.md and docs/video-training.md.
